ops.title: capt-hook: re-gate the graphite pre-submit review hook, which ccx.nogt now silences
ops.description:
Making `GraphiteActive` honor `ccx.nogt` (captain-hook, `captain_hook/util/vcs.py` `graphite_lane`) correctly softened all four graphite hooks. Three of them should soften. The fourth should not.

`builtin_packs/graphite/hooks/vcs.py:67-91` is the pre-submit review gate: it fires on `gt submit` / `gt s` / `gt ss` / `ccx vcs ship` and quiets once a cc-review pass has run in the session. Its rule — "approval to write the code is not approval to submit it" — is lane-independent. But `ccx vcs ship` is the ship command on the jj and plain-git lanes too, so the nogt fix turned that gate off in every `ccx.nogt` repo, cc-context included.

Accepted deliberately (2026-08-19) to keep the nogt fix single-purpose, rather than silently doing both.

The obvious fix is not safe as-is: dropping `GraphiteActive()` from that hook's `only_if` leaves it scoped by `Runs("gt","submit")` / `Runs("ccx","vcs","ship")` alone — but the graphite pack is in `UNCONDITIONAL_BUILTINS` (`captain_hook/packs/manager.py:41`), so the gate would then fire in EVERY repo on the machine, not just graphite ones. That is a real blast radius and needs its own test matrix.

Options worth weighing: (a) a new condition matching "a repo where ccx vcs ship is the ship command" rather than "a graphite repo"; (b) move the review gate out of the graphite pack into a lane-independent one; (c) gate it on `is_graphite_repo` (the marker fact) rather than `graphite_lane` (the policy), which restores today's behavior exactly at the cost of two predicates in one pack.

ops.text: The pre-submit review gate fires on `ccx vcs ship` in a repo that sets ccx.nogt
It does not fire in unrelated repositories that have never used gt or ccx
The other three graphite hooks still honor ccx.nogt and stay silent there
A test covers the ccx.nogt + review-gate combination in tests/test_pack_graphite.py
